analysis.title: Nordic Alert: US midterm elections – a referendum on Trump
key_insights: US equities closed lower on Nov 2 (Nasdaq -1.1%, S&P 500 -0.5%), driven by tech sector concerns. A near 8% drop in oil did not offset the decline.
Oil fell almost 8% on reports that Iran's supreme leader opened the door to indirect talks with the US. Brent trades around USD 105 per barrel.
Reports of possible US strikes on Iran after the midterms continue, but Trump has signalled he wants to give diplomacy more time. The US struck the Iranian island of Qeshm on Nov 2.
Apple reported fiscal Q3 EPS of USD 2.10 after the close on Nov 2, above expectations, while China revenue disappointed.

US midterms are today. All 435 House seats and 35 Senate seats are at stake. Betting markets give Democrats 96% odds of winning the House and 74% for the Senate. Results may be known by Wednesday morning Swedish time, and a close result could delay the count by a day or more.
The RBA raised its policy rate to 4.85% as expected, its fifth hike this year, to curb inflation.

US ISM manufacturing for October was stronger than expected. JOLTS for September is due today, with labour demand softening but no clear rise in voluntary resignations, consistent with firms cautious on hiring but retaining staff.
Russian and Ukrainian delegations meet in Abu Dhabi on Nov 10-11 with US mediation. Witkoff says talks will focus on post-war security arrangements, de-escalation and humanitarian issues.
Swedish industrial unions demand 3.9% wage increases under a one-year deal. SEB notes past experience suggests they could secure about 75% of the initial demand, around 3%, with wage drift on top.
